notes: ACCESS: Tier 1 (direct HTTP) blocked — curl and a headless Playwright/Chromium fetch with realistic browser headers both got Akamai 'Access Denied' 403 on www.kohls.com/ and /robots.txt (AkamaiGHost edge block, consistent on both attempts). Per hard-block rule, escalated straight to Tier 3 (Claude-in-Chrome, real logged-in browser session) which loaded the site normally (no robots.txt Claude-disallow found — robots.txt itself was unreachable under the Akamai block, so no opt-out signal existed to check). All extraction done via Claude-in-Chrome. DISCOVERY: Main site nav (Home & Pet, Women, Men, Baby, Kids & Toys, Shoes, Beauty, Jewelry, Handbags, Sports Fan, Gift Ideas, Sale & Clearance, College, Back to School, New & Trending) has no Christmas/Holiday/Seasonal item. Drilled into Home & Pet -> 'For the Home' (13 categories: Clearance, Kitchen & Dining, Bedding, Bath, Home Decor, Rugs, Window Treatments, Furniture, Floor Care, Electronics, Storage, Luggage, Pet) -> Home Decor department's 'Show All 15 Categories' grid, which surfaced two live seasonal/occasion nodes: Halloween and Fall (plus non-seasonal Neutrals/Patio & Outdoor/Character Shop, excluded). Checked for Christmas/Thanksgiving specifically via direct URL-pattern guesses mirroring the working Halloween/Fall URLs (christmas-for-the-home.jsp, christmas-decorative-accents-home-decor.jsp, thanksgiving-for-the-home.jsp) — all redirected to the homepage or a fallback page, confirming they are not live nodes right now. Also ran a site search for 'christmas decor' which returned 20,125 results — a non-discriminating, near-catalog-wide count typical of Kohl's search (does not filter to a real category), so per the shared 'search is not proof' rule this was NOT used as evidence of a Christmas category; only the confirmed-dead direct URLs and absent nav items were used to conclude Christmas/Thanksgiving/Valentine's/Easter/New Year/Diwali are not currently presented as genuine categories on this US general-merchandise site (snapshot taken 2026-09-04; Kohl's evidently activates each seasonal hub only when the shopping window opens — Halloween and Fall are the two live now). SCOPE: captured only Home/Pet department seasonal nodes (Occasion:Halloween/Fall + Activity:For the Home), not fashion/costumes/apparel. STRUCTURE: Both Halloween and Fall present as an umbrella 'For the Home' PLP (own real qty) whose 'Show All Categories' grid breaks into per-product-type PLPs (Decorative Accents, Kitchen & Dining, Bedding & Bath, Artificial Flowers & Plants, Throw Pillows, Rugs, Wall Decor, Candles, +Pet Supplies for Halloween). Modeled each holiday's umbrella page as a grouping row (qty/link null) with the product-type pages as leaf rows, per the parent/child rule. Note: the leaf quantities do not sum exactly to the umbrella page's displayed total (Halloween: children sum ~1942 vs umbrella 1780; similar for Fall) because the site's facet tags overlap (one product can carry more than one subcategory tag) — this is normal sibling overlap, not a double-count by this extraction. Halloween Pet Supplies is included per the Seasonal category's explicit coexistence rule (a Pet-department product may also be a valid Seasonal row) even though it would also belong to the Pet Care workbook. Fall is included as a genuine seasonal/occasion category per the ruleset's 'Autumn/Fall' allowance in 'other genuine seasonal events' — Kohl's own taxonomy tags it with an 'Occasion:Fall' facet exactly like Halloween, and its own copy ('Fall decor for homes with hosting to do') frames it as a seasonal decorating event, not a generic style/trend. All qty figures are the exact PLP-displayed count ('Category Name (N)') as of 2026-09-04.
